snippet.title: How Michael Jackson Risked Everything Trying to Top Thriller | Bad World Tour | the detail.
snippet.description:
Following the unprecedented success of 'Thriller', Michael Jackson had conquered the music world. But the King of Pop faced an almost impossible challenge: how could he surpass the biggest-selling album in history, break free from his family's shadow, and prove that he could succeed entirely on his own?

In Part 1 of our four-part documentary series, 'Michael Jackson's BAD World Tour: Everything to Prove, Everything to Lose', we explore the extraordinary events that led to opening night of Michael Jackson's first solo concert tour in 1987.

From the bitter controversies surrounding The Jacksons' 1984 Victory Tour and his increasingly strained relationship with the Jackson family to the unprecedented pressure of following 'Thriller,' Michael was determined to establish himself as the world's greatest solo entertainer.

As he built an independent entertainment empire, Michael embarked on an ambitious period of creative reinvention. His groundbreaking acquisition of the Beatles' ATV music catalogue, Disney's 'Captain EO', and his growing fascination with filmmaking were all part of a much larger vision for his future.

But behind the scenes, the creation of his long-awaited follow up album to 'Thriller' was proving far more complicated than anticipated. Working alongside legendary producer Quincy Jones, Michael spent years attempting to create a worthy successor. Meanwhile, mounting delays, increasingly hostile media coverage, rumours about his changing appearance and enormous commercial expectations threatened to overshadow his comeback before it had even begun.

snippet.title: Michael Jackson & Madonna: Their Rivalry, Romance & Fallout Revealed | the detail.
snippet.description:
Michael Jackson and Madonna were the King and Queen of Pop, but behind their legendary careers was a complicated relationship of admiration, rivalry, romance, creative conflict and eventual regret.

In this complete documentary, we explore the extraordinary history between Michael Jackson and Madonna, from Madonna's early admiration for Michael during the Thriller era to her emergence as one of his greatest commercial rivals and their surprising private relationship in the early 1990s.

While Michael was recording in 1991, he approached Madonna about a potential collaboration. The two began spending time together privately, appeared at The Ivy in Los Angeles and famously attended the 1991 Academy Awards together. Their planned collaboration on “In the Closet”, however, exposed just how different the two superstars really were. 

The collaboration collapsed, their friendship deteriorated and stories began emerging of disagreements and Michael's alleged private criticisms of Madonna. Yet their story didn't end there. Years later, Madonna would publicly defend Michael during one of the darkest periods of his career — and following his death in 2009, admitted that she regretted allowing him to disappear from her life.

From Thriller and Like a Virgin to Bad, Like a Prayer, Dangerous and the 1991 Oscars, this is the complete story of two radically different artists who helped redefine modern superstardom and the unusual relationship that developed between the King and Queen of Pop.

snippet.title: Slash On Michael Jackson’s Private World: “Nobody Was Real” | the detail.
snippet.description:
Slash opens up about his extraordinary experiences working with Michael Jackson, from receiving an unexpected phone call from the King of Pop to recording together, appearing alongside him on stage and witnessing Michael’s legendary perfectionism firsthand.

The Guns N’ Roses guitarist reflects on recording 'Give In to Me' for Michael Jackson’s Dangerous album, his involvement with 'Black or White,' their unforgettable live performances and what Michael was really like behind the scenes. Slash also shares his thoughts on Michael Jackson’s private world, the isolation that came with his extraordinary fame, and why he believes people around Michael often took advantage of him.

Through Slash’s own words, discover the untold story of one of music’s most unlikely collaborations and his memories of Michael Jackson as an artist, performer and person.

snippet.description:
In this video, members of the Jackson family recount the heartbreaking final days of Michael Jackson's life. His siblings describe the last time they saw him, the final conversations they shared, where they were when they heard the devastating news, and the emotional moments that followed his passing on 25 June 2009.

Featuring rare interviews with Jermaine Jackson, Tito Jackson, Janet Jackson and other members of the Jackson family, this documentary explores Michael Jackson's final family gathering, his excitement ahead of the This Is It concerts at London's O2 Arena, the frantic journey to UCLA Medical Center, and the lasting impact his death had on those closest to him.

Beyond the tragedy of his passing, Michael Jackson's siblings reflect on his extraordinary legacy as an entertainer, humanitarian, father and brother. snippet.title: Michael Jackson Fired Him... But Now John Branca Controls His Empire? | the detail.
snippet.description:
John Branca was one of the most influential figures in Michael Jackson's career. As Michael's entertainment lawyer, he helped negotiate record-breaking contracts, advised him on the purchase of the ATV Music Publishing catalogue, and played a key role in transforming Jackson from a global superstar into a powerful music industry businessman.

But despite years of success together, Michael Jackson abruptly fired John Branca. Their relationship broke down amid tensions with Sony Music, Tommy Mottola, and growing distrust within Michael's inner circle. Yet just years later, Branca returned to Michael's life during preparations for the This Is It concerts, only weeks before Jackson's death.

In this video, we explore the complete story of Michael Jackson and John Branca, from the success of Off The Wall, Thriller, Bad and the acquisition of the Beatles catalogue, to the Sony Music deal, the child molestation allegations, Michael's financial troubles, and the creation of one of the most successful celebrity estates in history.

This is the story of the lawyer who helped build Michael Jackson's empire, was removed from the inner circle, and ultimately returned to shape his legacy for generations to come.

snippet.title: Comparing Every Michael Jackson Biopic Ever Made | the detail.
snippet.description:
For more than 30 years, Hollywood has repeatedly attempted to recreate, reinterpret, and understand Michael Jackson. But every Michael Jackson biopic reveals just as much about the era in which it was made as it does about the man himself.

From the family-approved nostalgia of The Jacksons: An American Dream, to the tabloid-fuelled VH1 drama Man in the Mirror, to the more intimate and sympathetic portrayal presented in Searching for Neverland, and finally the enormous estate-backed spectacle of 2026’s Michael; each project presents a completely different version of Michael Jackson shaped by the public imagination of its time.

In this documentary, we explore every major Michael Jackson biopic ever made, analysing how Hollywood attempted to capture the King of Pop across different decades of fame, controversy, mythology, and cultural reinvention. We examine who was controlling the narrative behind each production, how the media shaped public perception of Michael Jackson, and why his story continues to be rewritten for every new generation.

snippet.title: Michael Jackson Is One of the Most Streamed Artists in the World… Again #michaeljackson #mj
snippet.description:
Following the release of the 2026 Michael biopic, Billie Jean surged to over 6 million Spotify streams PER DAY, with Beat It approaching 5 million daily streams globally.

Michael’s catalogue is now generating roughly 55–60 million Spotify streams every single day — with younger audiences driving much of the resurgence.
What’s perhaps most fascinating is how the streaming era has reshaped his catalogue entirely. Songs like Human Nature and Smooth Criminal are now outperforming some of his biggest original chart hits from the 1990s.

The music industry has changed completely since Michael’s peak… yet somehow his catalogue continues to compete with modern artists nearly half a century  later.#michaeljackson #mj #michaelmovie #thejacksons #jackson5 #billiejean #thriller

snippet.title: A Mother’s Regret: Katherine Jackson on Michael’s Childhood & Death (Full Documentary) | the detail.
snippet.description:
'A Mother’s Regret' is a powerful and emotional full documentary told in the words of Katherine Jackson, the mother of the legendary Michael Jackson. In this rare and intimate account, Katherine reflects on her son’s extraordinary life, his painful struggles, and the tragic day the world lost the King of Pop.

Through her heartfelt memories, Katherine shares what Michael was like as a child full of energy and talent, how he rose to global fame, and the price he paid with a lost childhood. She speaks candidly about Joe Jackson’s strict parenting, Michael’s shyness off stage, the discipline that many later called abuse, and how fame often left her son feeling like “an animal in a cage.”

Katherine also addresses the most difficult moments in Michael’s life: the plastic surgery rumors, his battle with vitiligo, the cruel “Wacko Jacko” label, and the devastating allegations. With unwavering love, she defends her son’s innocence and character.

Finally, Katherine opens up about the day of June 25, 2009, the worst day of her life, when she was told Michael didn’t survive. She reveals her fears about the gruelling 'This Is It' tour schedule, his dependency on painkillers after the Pepsi accident, and the unanswered questions that still haunt her till this day.

snippet.title: Michael Jackson’s Voice Was a Lie… But Here’s Why | the detail.
snippet.description:
For decades, fans have debated Michael Jackson’s real voice. Was the King of Pop’s soft, high-pitched speaking voice genuine, or was it something he deliberately created for the public? In this video we examine the truth about Michael Jackson’s speaking voice, exploring why many people close to him claimed he actually spoke with a much deeper, more commanding tone in private.

Drawing on rare interviews, recordings and testimony from those who knew him personally — including Spike Lee, Liza Minnelli, Quincy Jones and Lisa Marie Presley — we investigate the mystery behind Michael Jackson’s “real” voice and how it differed from the voice the world heard in public.

From his childhood in Gary, Indiana, through the rise of The Jackson 5, and into the peak of his solo career during albums like Off the Wall, Thriller, Dangerous and HIStory, this documentary explores how Jackson’s voice evolved over time. We look at how vocal training, media scrutiny, and the pressures of global fame may have influenced the way Michael Jackson spoke in interviews and public appearances.

We also examine the rumours and conspiracy theories that emerged over the years — including claims about chemical castration, vocal preservation, and deliberate “code switching” — and assess what the evidence actually suggests.

By analysing Jackson’s vocal range, speaking patterns, and rare moments where his deeper register appeared, this video reveals what Michael Jackson really sounded like behind the carefully constructed King of Pop persona.

snippet.title: The Real Story Behind Michael Jackson & Paul McCartney’s Beatles Catalog Feud | the detail.
snippet.description:
For a brief moment in the early 1980s, Michael Jackson and Paul McCartney stood side by side at the top of the music industry. Their collaborations on 'The Girl Is Mine' and 'Say Say Say' united two of the most successful artists of their respective generations — the rising King of Pop and one of the legendary songwriters of The Beatles. What began as admiration and creative partnership soon became one of the most famous rivalries in music history.

From their early friendship and musical collaborations to the moment Jackson purchased the ATV Music Publishing catalog containing Lennon–McCartney songs, the story reveals how business decisions, music publishing rights, and commercial ambition transformed a creative partnership into a bitter dispute. What started as a shared passion for songwriting ultimately became a clash between two of the most powerful figures in popular music.

Using rare interviews, archival footage, and historical context, this film examines how Michael Jackson came to own the Beatles catalog, why Paul McCartney felt betrayed by the deal, and how the business of music publishing changed the relationship between two global icons. It also explores the wider implications of the acquisition — including how the Beatles’ songs were licensed, how the catalog later became part of Sony/ATV Music Publishing, and how McCartney eventually regained rights to portions of his music decades later.

Michael Jackson and Paul McCartney’s story is more than just a business dispute. It is a case study in the power of music publishing, the economics of the recording industry, and the complicated relationship between friendship and commerce at the highest level of pop stardom.

Their collaborations on 'The Girl Is Mine' and 'Say Say Say' united two of the most successful artists of their respective generations — the rising King of Pop and one of the legendary songwriters of The Beatles. What began as admiration and creative partnership soon became one of the most famous rivalries in music history.

From their early friendship and musical collaborations to the moment Jackson purchased the ATV Music Publishing catalog containing Lennon–McCartney songs, the story reveals how business decisions, music publishing rights, and commercial ambition transformed a creative partnership into a bitter dispute. What started as a shared passion for songwriting ultimately became a clash between two of the most powerful figures in popular music.

Using rare interviews, archival footage, and historical context, this film examines how Michael Jackson came to own the Beatles catalog, why Paul McCartney felt betrayed by the deal, and how the business of music publishing changed the relationship between two global icons. It also explores the wider implications of the acquisition — including how the Beatles’ songs were licensed, how the catalog later became part of Sony/ATV Music Publishing, and how McCartney eventually regained rights to portions of his music decades later.

Michael Jackson and Paul McCartney’s story is more than just a business dispute. It is a case study in the power of music publishing, the economics of the recording industry, and the complicated relationship between friendship and commerce at the highest level of pop stardom.

snippet.title: Katherine Jackson Breaks Silence on Michael’s Surgery, Sexuality, and Allegations | the detail.
snippet.description:

snippet.title: 1977 | Michael Jackson's Year In Review | the detail.
snippet.description:
1977 was pivotal year for Michael Jackson, as he made his first real effort to branch out and seek solo stardom after releasing two albums with Epic with his brothers under the Jacksons. In this effort, Michael accepted the role of the scarecrow in the film adaption of 'The Wiz' and moved to New York to start filming. 

It was the first time he was able get out from under his father's grip and start living his life as a young adult, after many years being treated like one. During the filming he formed a bond with producer Quincy Jones and started plans a reinvigorate his music career as a solo artist.

After 6 years of non-stop recording, promoting, and performing, the Jackson 5 were getting wary with their Motown management. Their records weren't selling like they used to, the group wanted more creative control and most importantly more of their bottomline. 

In March 1976, The Jackson 5 became the Jacksons as the group switched from Motown to Epic records. Leaving brother Jermaine back at Motown and picking up brother Randy and sisters Rebbie, La Toya and Janet for the family's Las Vegas show and primetime variety show on CBS. But can they achieve the same level of success outside of Motown's management? And how much longer can the brother survive in this showbiz hamster wheel?

snippet.title: Where ‘We Are The World’ Charity Donations REALLY Went | the detail.
snippet.description:
Where did donations from USA for Africa's charity single actually go? 

'We Are The World' was written by Michael Jackson and Lionel Richie and released to raise funds for the Ethiopian famine, which had reached its peak in the mid 1980s. Its sky-high sales and the tens of millions of dollars raised was championed as a huge success at the time, but what effect did the newly-founded charitable foundation have on the ongoing crisis? 

The sad truth is that much of the money given in good faith to save many lives ended up being used to help Ethiopia's dictator and fund nonsensical wars across the troubled country.

snippet.title: Michael Jackson Meets The Simpsons | The FULL Story Behind His Episode! | the detail.
snippet.description:
Michael Jackson was a fan of The Simpsons as soon as they launched onto tv screens back in 1989. So much so he rang up the cartoon creators and straight off the bat offered to write Bart a number one single and guest star in the show. 

The single was 'Do The Bartman', released in 1990, in which Jackson co-wrote and did back up vocals for, and The Simpsons episode he appeared in was Season Three's debut 'Stark Raving Dad'. 

Michael Jackson would be referenced several times throughout the series longstanding run, before allegations made against the King Of Pop motivated The Simpsons creators to remove their episode with Jackson and cut all ties with the superstar.

snippet.title: How Jermaine Jackson Got CANCELLED & Almost Lost Everything!?! | the detail.
snippet.description:
Jermaine Jackson was riding on a career high after the success of the Emmy winning mini series 'The Jacksons: An American Dream', when his brother Michael's life went into turmoil after being accused of child abuse in the summer of 1993. Jermaine and his whole family rallied round Michael to get him through the allegations, in hopes he would pay them back by appearing in their Jackson Honors TV special. 

However, the family overpromised leaving fans and executives disappointed with the programmes final outcome, resulting in a legal, personal and career downturn for Jermaine. Maybe he could make a final comeback with a reunion with his brothers? But crucially would Michael join them as well?

snippet.title: 2009 | Michael Jackson's Year In Review | the detail.
snippet.description:
2009 was set to be the King of Pop's triumphant comeback to the stage, with a series of concerts announced at London's O2 arena, 'This Is It' was said to be Michael Jackson's final curtain call before retiring from performing all together. The demand for tickets were insatiable and the original 10 concerts ballooned to 50 due to the incredible demand. 

Nearly a million ticket holders paid to watch Michael Jackson moonwalk across his legendary stage one more time, in what was considered one of the most elaborate and ambitious productions in music history. Michael Jackson was gearing up to give the performance of a lifetime, silencing his critics once and for all, before tragic struck and the world mourned for the loss of a true musical icon never to be seen again.

snippet.description:

snippet.title: Did Michael Jackson Ever Give Beatles Songs Back To Paul McCartney?! | the detail.
snippet.description:
Michael Jackson famously acquired the rights to the Beatles music catalog in the 1980s, which, as a result, amassed a huge amount of wealth over the years for the King of Pop. Music publishing, a venture Paul McCartney reportedly advised him to get into in the first place and felt betrayed when Jackson bought the songs the ex-Beatle lost many years before. 

Tension built as the two music icons fought each other as to how the legendary music would be licensed and, maybe more importantly, who got a bigger portion of the profit. But after Jackson's death in 2009, many speculated what would happen to the catalog next.

Who's hands is the catalog now in? What its value today? And has Paul McCartney ever been able to gain control of his music since?
